full_judgment:
This Rule at the instance of the appellant-petitioner was issued under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, calling upon the respondent-opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the Judgment and order No. 60 dated 18-10-1993, passed by the Additional District Judge, Narayanganj, in Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1992 allowing the application of the opposite party No. 1 under Order XLI rule 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure, should not be set aside. 

 2. The case of the petitioner, in short, is that the opposite party Nos.1 to 3 were the joint mutawallis in respect of Panch Peer Darga Waqf Estate bearing Ex No. 6831 of village Bhagalpur, police station, Sonargaon, in the District of Narayanganj. The aforesaid local musallis of the area being dissatisfied with the functions of the aforesaid joint mutawalli held a meeting on 11-7-1982 and formed a committee consisting of 7 persons with the petitioner Shahabuddin Ahmed as its Secretary for proper maintenance, better management and administration of the waqf estate and also to take appropriate steps in accordance with law for removal of the said joint mutawallis, the opposite party Nos. 1 to 3. Accordingly, this petitioner presented an. application on 7-8-1982 before the Administrator of Waqf under section 32(1) of Waqf Ordinance for removal of the said opposite party Nos. 1 to 3 as joint mutawallis, alleging breach of trust, mismanagement, malfeasance and misappropriation of- funds. The aforesaid joint mutawallis contested the said application for their removal by filing a joint written objection on 15-9-1982 denying all material allegations. The Administrator of Waqfs on taking evidence adduced by both the parties, dismissed the application brought by this petitioner by his order dated 26-10-1987 in EC No. 6831. Thereafter the petitioner filed an appeal before the learned District Judge, Narayanganj, being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 7 of 1989. In due course the said appeal was heard ex parte, by the learned Additional District Judge, and by his judgment and order dated 11-11-1991 allowed the appeal and set aside the order dated 26-10-1987 passed by the Administrator of Waqfs. Thereafter, ten months twenty days, later on 1-10-1992, the opposite party No. 1 filed a Miscellaneous case being Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1992 under Order XLI rule 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure, praying for setting aside the earlier ex parte order, on the ground inter alia, for non-service of summons upon him. After hearing, the learned District Judge, Narayanganj, by his order No. 60 dated 18-10-1993 allowed the said miscellaneous case and set aside the earlier ex parte order dated 11-1-1991. Being aggrieved, this petitioner obtained the present Rule under section 115 of the, Code of Civil Procedure. 

 4. Mr Mir Mahfuzur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the opposite party Nos. 1, 2 and 3 were brothers and joint mutawallis of the concerned waqf properties. On receipt of the notice, in connection with the application under section 32 of the Waqf Ordinance, they duly appeared before the Administrator of Waqfs and contested the case against them by filing a joint written statement denying all allegations against them, that after dismissal of the said application an appeal was filed and notices of the appeal was also duly served upon them through process server as well as by post. The learned Advocate, referring to Annexures-A and B, submits that according to the report of the process server, the opposite party Nos. 1 to 3 were not at home at the relevant time, as such, their mother who used to live with them received the said summons on their behalf and the opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 duly appeared in Court on 30-3-1989 which-shows that their mother duly informed her sons, the opposite party Nos. 1 to 3, that the summons was also issued through registered post with acknowledgment due but the one issued to the opposite party No. 1 was returned by the postal peon with an endorsement 'refused', which tantamount to, proper service, that though the opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 duly appeared in Court that although they, as joint mutawallis, contested before the Administrator of Waqfs but they ultimately, did not contest the appeal as such, the learned Additional District Judge after hearing allowed the appeal. As such, the learned Advocate submits, there was due and proper service of summons on the respondent-opposite party Nos.1 to 3 and the learned Appellant Judge committed an error of law in ignoring the report of the process server on the copy of the summons and his declaration dated 5-3-1989 and the endorsement of the postal peon on the, letter containing the summons and illegally allowed the Miscellaneous case which has occasioned a failure of justice. On such grounds he prays for making the Rule absolute and dismissing the miscellaneous case. 

 6. I have heard the learned Advocates of both sides and examined the records. It appears that the opposite party Nos. 1 to 3 were joint mutawallis of a waqf estate. They contested the case against them before the Administrator of Waqfs by filing a Joint written statement. In appeal in the Court of District Judge, the summons upon all the respondents were duly issued and the report of the process server shows that the respondent Nos. 1 to 3 were not at home when he reached there, as such, their mother received the summons on their behalf putting her left thumb impression upon the copy of the summons. The process server deposed as OPW 2 and proved his report and declaration. He denied the suggestions made on behalf of the opposite party No. 1 that he never went to their house to serve the summons. On the face of this evidence, the respondent-opposite party No. 1 neither examined his mother nor specifically challenged her finger impression as alleged by the process server as OPW 2. Under such circumstances, it can hardly be disputed that the process server served the summons on their mother, because on receipt of the said summons, the respondent Nos. 1 and 3 (the opposite party Nos. 2 and 3) duly appeared in the appeal. As such, the summons was at least received by the mother of the respondent Nos. 1 to 3 who was available at the relevant time in their address, has been proved. The deposition of the petitioner (as OPW 1) shows that although the respondent No. 3 is the step-brother of the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 but they are brothers and sons of one mother. It is true that the mother of the respondent No. 3 received the summons but if she could communicate the matter to her one step-son, the respondent No. 1 there was no reason, not to communicate the same to her another step-son, the respondent No. 2 opposite party No. 1. Besides, when the respondent No. 1 appeared in the appeal, it is difficult to believe that his own brother and joint mutawalli was not aware of the said appeal. 

 7. The summons were also issued to the respondent-opposite party No. 1 through registered post with acknowledgment due, but the said notice was returned with an endorsement refused by the postal peon. The learned Appellate Judge held that the summons issued through post was not actually delivered to the respondent-opposite party No. 1 as the postal peon was not examined by the appellant-petitioner. The learned Advocate on behalf of the petitioner submits that a letter issued under registered cover is presumed to be delivered unless proved otherwise by the addressee but the learned Appellate Judge committed an error of law in shifting the onus on him, instead of on the respondent-opposite party No. 1. He relies in this respect on section 114, illustration (f) of the Evidence Act and section 27 of the General Clauses Act. This submission of the learned Advocate has substance. If the letter is properly addressed and posted, proper service is to be presumed, and in the absence of any evidence to the contrary this fact is proved, unless it is proved otherwise by the addressee who may, however, prove with the onus lying upon him that the letter in question never reached him. Reliance in this regard may be placed' in the case of Hari Pada Dutta VS, Jay Gopal Mukherjee 39 CWN 934 in which their Lordships Rankin CJ and Person, J. have held that a summons sent by registered post and returned with the endorsement refused is prima facie evidence that the addressee had an opportunity to accept it and the service, thus effected, is therefore, a good and valid service and that to invalidate such a service the defendant must expressly prove to the satisfaction of the Court, that what would happen in the ordinary course did not happen and that he did not get an opportunity to accept it, and for that purpose it is open to him to prove that he never refused it and that it was never tendered to him, and that a mere denial that it was never delivered to him is not sufficient. 

 8. Besides, the respondent Nos. 1 to 3 were the joint mutawallis, and as such joint mutawallis they were required to act and' function jointly as they did in filing their joint written statement and contest the case before the Administrator of Waqfs, The respondent Nos. 1 and 3 though appeared before the Appellate Court on 30-10-1989 but even they did not take any steps after 20-11-1990 in the appeal and the learned Appellate Judge after giving ten adjournments because of their absence, ultimately heard the appeal ex parte on 9-11-1991 and delivered the judgment on 11-11-1991. 

 9. In view of the above facts and circumstances, the miscellaneous case filed under Order XLI rule 21 is liable to be rejected because the respondent-opposite party No. 1 failed to discharge his onus that in spite of issuing the summons through registered post with acknowledgment due, as required under sub-rule 2 of rule 19B of Order V of the Code of Civil Procedure, the said notice actually did not reach him and since in spite of appearance of the respondent No. 1 who is his own brother and respondent No.3 who is his step-brother, in court and who were also his joint mutawallis, still he was not aware of the appeal and, as such, the learned, appellate Judge committed an error of law in allowing the miscellaneous case which occasioned a failure of justice; as the respondent-opposite party failed to prove that the notice was not duly served or that he was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing when the appeal was called on for hearing. Accordingly the judgment and order of the learned Additional District Judge, in Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1992, is set aside.
